title: Geography Lec 3
summary: India's river systems fall into two groups: Himalayan (perennial, glacier-fed, long and deep courses) and Peninsular (seasonal, monsoon-dependent, short and shallow).
Antecedent rivers: Indus, Sutlej, Kosi, Brahmaputra - older than the Himalayan uplift, they cut through the mountains to maintain their courses.
Northern Plains: Bhabar (8-16 km), Terai, Khadar (new alluvium), Bhangar (old alluvium); total length about 3200 km, about 2400 km in India.

Indus: rises from the Bokhar Chu glacier (Singi Khamban in Tibet); right-bank tributaries - Shyok, Gilgit, Kabul, Swat, Gomal, Tochi; the Panjnad joins it at Mithankot; Chenab is its largest tributary.
Panch Prayag (DV PK MR BD): Vishnuprayag-Dhauliganga, Nandprayag-Nandakini, Karnaprayag-Pindar, Rudraprayag-Mandakini, Devprayag-Bhagirathi; the Ganga begins at Devprayag.
Brahmaputra: Chemayungdung -> Tsangpo -> Siang/Dihang -> Brahmaputra -> Jamuna; Majuli is the largest river island; Farakka (Ganga Water) Treaty 1996, barrage 1975.
Left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi; right-bank: Yamuna, Son, Punpun; Kosi is the 'Sorrow of Bihar'.
Passes: Rohtang (Manali-Lahaul), Bara-lacha La (to Leh), Zoji La (Srinagar-Leh), Burzil (to Gilgit), Banihal (to Jammu); Atal Tunnel is 9.02 km long.
Dams: Tehri (Bhagirathi, highest), Bhakra (highest gravity dam), Hirakud (longest, Sambalpur), Srisailam/Nagarjuna Sagar (Krishna), Mettur (Kaveri).
National Waterways: NW-1 Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly (Prayagraj-Haldia, 1620 km), NW-2 Brahmaputra, NW-3 Kerala, NW-4 Godavari-Krishna, NW-5 Mahanadi, NW-6 Barak.
Peninsular rivers: Narmada (Amarkantak) and Tapti (Betul) flow west through rift valleys; Godavari is the largest (Trimbakeshwar); Krishna (Mahabaleshwar); Kaveri (Talakaveri).

Tributary tricks: Godavari - Manjira, Sabari, Purna, Penganga, Pranhita, Wainganga, Wardha, Indravati; Krishna - Bhima, Tungabhadra, Musi, Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Dudhganga; Mahanadi - Ong, Jonk, Tel, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib.
Drainage patterns: dendritic (Himalayan rivers), trellis (right-angle junctions), radial (Amarkantak), centripetal (Loktak Lake); the Chambal is famous for its ravines (badlands).
Monsoon: from the Arabic 'mausim'; heated Tibet -> low pressure -> tropical easterly jet, Coriolis force; Mascarene High; the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches merge over the Punjab plains.
The retreating/north-east monsoon brings rain to the Coromandel Coast; Western Disturbances (from the Mediterranean) help rabi crops; El Nino reduces rainfall, La Nina increases it.
Pre-monsoon showers: Kalbaisakhi (Bengal), Bardoli Chheerha (Assam), Mango Showers and Blossom Showers (Kerala-Karnataka); Pune lies in a rain-shadow area; the Western Ghats get over 200 cm of rain.

mcqs.q: What is the nature of Himalayan rivers?
mcqs.e: Himalayan rivers are fed by glaciers, so they flow throughout the year.

mcqs.q: Peninsular rivers are generally:
mcqs.e: Their flow depends on monsoon rainfall; they have no glacial source.

mcqs.q: In the context of rivers, the term 'ephemeral' refers to:
mcqs.e: An ephemeral river is seasonal and flows only during the rainy season.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Himalayan rivers is correct?
o: They carry water only in the rainy season
Their courses are short and shallow
Their courses are long and deep
mcqs.e: It is the Peninsular rivers that have short and shallow courses.

mcqs.q: What is the correct meaning of an 'antecedent' river?
o: A river that drains only into the east coast
A river that rises in the east
A river that existed before the Himalayan uplift and cut through the mountains to keep its course
mcqs.e: Antecedent does not mean east-flowing; examples are the Indus, Sutlej and Kosi.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an antecedent river?
mcqs.e: The Indus, Sutlej, Brahmaputra and Kosi are antecedent rivers.

mcqs.q: The Northern Plains of India were formed mainly by which three river systems?
mcqs.e: The total length of the Northern Plains is about 3200 km.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate length of the Northern Plains within India?
mcqs.e: The entire Northern Plains are 3200 km long, of which about 2400 km lie in India.

mcqs.q: What is the width of the Bhabar belt?
mcqs.e: In the Bhabar, rivers disappear among pebbles and boulders.

mcqs.q: The narrow belt at the foot of the Shiwaliks where rivers disappear among pebbles is called:
mcqs.e: South of the Bhabar lies the marshy Terai, where the rivers re-emerge.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic feature of the Terai region?
mcqs.e: Rivers that vanish in the Bhabar reappear in the Terai.

mcqs.q: What is new alluvial soil called?
mcqs.e: Khadar is new alluvium of the floodplains; Bhangar is old alluvium.

mcqs.q: What is old alluvial soil called?
mcqs.e: Bhangar lies on higher ground beyond the reach of floodwaters.

mcqs.q: The Indus rises from which glacier?
mcqs.e: It lies in Tibet near Kailash-Mansarovar.

mcqs.q: What is the Indus called in Tibet?
mcqs.e: Singi Khamban means 'Lion's Mouth'.

mcqs.q: Which is a right-bank tributary of the Indus?
mcqs.e: Right-bank tributaries: Shyok, Gilgit, Kabul, Swat, Gomal, Tochi.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a left-bank tributary of the Indus?
mcqs.e: Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (Panjnad) and Zanskar join on the left bank.

mcqs.q: The Nubra river is a tributary of:
mcqs.e: The Nubra joins the Shyok, not the Indus directly.

mcqs.q: The world's highest railway bridge in Jammu and Kashmir is built over which river?
mcqs.e: The Chenab Rail Bridge is 359 m high (USBRL project).

mcqs.q: What is the approximate height of the Chenab Rail Bridge?
mcqs.e: It is taller than the Eiffel Tower.

mcqs.q: Which dams are built on the Chenab?
mcqs.e: Baglihar, Dulhasti and Salal are on the Chenab.

mcqs.q: The Tulbul and Kishanganga projects are associated with which river?
mcqs.e: Tulbul is at Wular Lake on the Jhelum; the Kishanganga is a Jhelum tributary.

mcqs.q: The Pong Dam is located on which river?
mcqs.e: Pong Dam is on the Beas in Himachal Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which river rises from the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh in Uttarkashi district?
mcqs.e: The Bhagirathi rises from the Gangotri glacier at Gaumukh.

mcqs.q: The Alaknanda rises from which glacier?
mcqs.e: The Satopanth glacier is near Badrinath.

mcqs.q: The Mandakini rises from which glacier?
mcqs.e: The Mandakini flows past Kedarnath.

mcqs.q: Which river joins the Alaknanda at Vishnuprayag?
mcqs.e: Remember 'DV PK MR BD': Dhauli-Vishnu, Nandakini-Nand, Pindar-Karna, Mandakini-Rudra, Bhagirathi-Dev.

mcqs.q: Which river joins the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag?
mcqs.e: Pindar + Alaknanda = Karnaprayag.

mcqs.q: Nandprayag is the confluence of which rivers?
mcqs.e: Nandakini -> Nandprayag.

mcqs.q: Rudraprayag is the confluence of which rivers?
mcqs.e: Mandakini -> Rudraprayag.

mcqs.q: The Ganga is formed at Devprayag by the confluence of:
mcqs.e: Below Devprayag the river is called the Ganga.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of the Panch Prayag (upstream to downstream)?
mcqs.e: These five confluences lie in this order along the Alaknanda.

mcqs.q: The Yamuna rises from a glacier in which range?
mcqs.e: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj.

mcqs.q: The 'Triveni Sangam' at Prayagraj is the confluence of which rivers?
mcqs.e: The Saraswati is not visible today.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest tributary of the Ganga?
mcqs.e: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a tributary of the Yamuna?
mcqs.e: Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra; Son and Gomti are tributaries of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: Which are the right-bank tributaries of the Yamuna?
mcqs.e: The Tons and Hindon join it from the left.

mcqs.q: The Hindon, which joins near Noida, is a tributary of:
mcqs.e: The Tons joins the Yamuna within Uttarakhand itself.

mcqs.q: Which are the right-bank tributaries of the Ganga?
mcqs.e: The Son rises at Amarkantak and joins the Ganga in Bihar.

mcqs.q: Which are the left-bank tributaries of the Ganga?
mcqs.e: The Mahananda is also a left-bank tributary, though less important.

mcqs.q: Which river basin in India has the highest population density?
mcqs.e: The Ganga basin covers Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal.

mcqs.q: Which river forms deep gorges in the Himalaya and takes a U-turn near Namcha Barwa?
mcqs.e: China is planning a mega dam here, larger than the Three Gorges.

mcqs.q: The Brahmaputra rises from which glacier?
mcqs.e: It lies near Kailash-Mansarovar.

mcqs.q: By what name is the Brahmaputra known in Tibet?
mcqs.e: In Arunachal Pradesh it is called the Siang/Dihang.

mcqs.q: By what name is the Brahmaputra known in Arunachal Pradesh?
mcqs.e: After entering Assam it is called the Brahmaputra.

mcqs.q: What is the Brahmaputra called in Bangladesh?
mcqs.e: The Ganga is called the Padma in Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: What is the Ganga called in Bangladesh?
mcqs.e: The combined Padma-Jamuna later joins the Meghna.

mcqs.q: Which distributary of the Ganga branches off at Farakka?
mcqs.e: A tributary joins the main river; a distributary branches off from it.

mcqs.q: What is a distributary?
o: A stream that rises from a glacier
A channel that branches off from the main river
A stream that drains into a lake
A stream that joins the main river
mcqs.e: The Hooghly is a distributary of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: When was the Farakka Agreement (Ganga Water Treaty) signed?
mcqs.e: It was signed between the governments of India and Bangladesh.

mcqs.q: When was the Farakka Barrage commissioned?
mcqs.e: Farakka is in West Bengal; the Hooghly branches off here.

mcqs.q: Where does the Barak river originate?
mcqs.e: The Barak is a tributary of the Meghna.

mcqs.q: The Barakar river is a tributary of:
mcqs.e: Do not confuse the Barak with the Barakar.

mcqs.q: Which are left-bank tributaries of the Brahmaputra?
mcqs.e: Subansiri, Kameng, Manas, Teesta and Jaldhaka join on the right bank.

mcqs.q: The Teesta, a tributary of the Brahmaputra, originates in which state?
mcqs.e: Gurudongmar Lake is in Sikkim.

mcqs.q: Where is Gurudongmar Lake located?
mcqs.e: It is among the highest lakes in the world (about 5430 m).

mcqs.q: Majuli, the world's largest river island, lies in which river?
mcqs.e: Majuli is in Assam.

mcqs.q: Which is the most important right-bank tributary of the Spiti river?
mcqs.e: Pin Valley National Park is in Himachal Pradesh; the Spiti is a tributary of the Sutlej.

mcqs.q: Where do the Chandra and Bhaga meet to form the Chandrabhaga (Chenab)?
mcqs.e: Tandi is in Lahaul and Spiti district.

mcqs.q: Which pass connects Manali with Lahaul and Spiti?
mcqs.e: The Atal Tunnel was built to bypass the Rohtang Pass.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the Atal Tunnel?
mcqs.e: The Atal Tunnel runs beneath Rohtang in the eastern Pir Panjal range.

mcqs.q: The Ravi and Beas rivers originate near which pass?
mcqs.e: The Beas rises at Beas Kund near Rohtang.

mcqs.q: Which pass is used to travel from Lahaul and Spiti to Leh?
mcqs.e: The Chenab (Chandra) rises near Bara-lacha La.

mcqs.q: The Chenab is considered to originate near which pass?
mcqs.e: The Chandra and Bhaga unite to form the Chandrabhaga.

mcqs.q: Which pass connects the Kashmir Valley with Leh?
mcqs.e: Zoji La lies on the Srinagar-Leh route.

mcqs.q: Which pass leads from Kashmir (Srinagar) towards Gilgit (PoK)?
mcqs.e: The Burzil Pass lies on the Srinagar-Gilgit route.

mcqs.q: Which pass is used to go from the Kashmir Valley to Jammu?
mcqs.e: The Banihal Pass is in the Pir Panjal range.

mcqs.q: The Srisailam Dam is located on which river?
mcqs.e: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is also on the Krishna.

mcqs.q: The Mettur Dam is located on which river?
mcqs.e: The Krishna Raja Sagara Dam is also on the Kaveri.

mcqs.q: The Tehri Dam is built on which river?
mcqs.e: Tehri is India's highest dam (earth and rockfill).

mcqs.q: Which is India's highest gravity dam?
mcqs.e: Bhakra Nangal is on the Sutlej.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest dam in India?
mcqs.e: The Hirakud Dam is on the Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: In which district is the Hirakud Dam located?
mcqs.e: The Mahanadi was once called the 'Sorrow of Odisha'.

mcqs.q: In which district is Lonar Lake located?
mcqs.e: Lonar is a saline lake formed by a meteorite impact.

mcqs.q: The Kosi river is known as the:
mcqs.e: It brings huge sediment from the Himalaya and shifts its course often.

mcqs.q: Why does the Kosi frequently change its course in the plains?
mcqs.e: Sediment deposition blocks the channel, forcing the river to shift course.

mcqs.q: The Gomti originates from which lake?
mcqs.e: The Gomti is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Ramganga is considered to originate in which mountain area?
mcqs.e: The Ramganga is a tributary of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: Where does the Ghaghara originate?
mcqs.e: Its tributary is the Kali (Sharda).

mcqs.q: The Gori Ganga is a tributary of which river?
mcqs.e: The Gori Ganga rises from the Milam glacier.

mcqs.q: Where does the Gandak originate?
mcqs.e: The Gandak is a left-bank tributary of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Arun Kosi and Sun Kosi are tributaries of:
mcqs.e: The Kosi originates near the Nepal-Tibet border.

mcqs.q: Why is the Hooghly called the 'Bhagirathi-Hooghly'?
o: This branch of the Ganga below Farakka is called the Bhagirathi-Hooghly
It is a branch of the Brahmaputra
It is the same Bhagirathi as at Devprayag
It is a tributary of the Alaknanda
mcqs.e: National Waterway-1 runs along the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-1 is on which river system?
mcqs.e: It is the longest national waterway.

mcqs.q: What is the stretch and length of National Waterway-1?
mcqs.e: It is India's longest national waterway.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-2 is on which river?
mcqs.e: It lies in Assam.

mcqs.q: Where is National Waterway-3 located?
mcqs.e: It is also called the West Coast Canal.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-4 is on which river system?
mcqs.e: It lies in South India.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-5 is associated with which river?
mcqs.e: It includes the East Coast Canal and the Brahmani-Mahanadi delta.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-6 is on which river?
mcqs.e: The Barak is a tributary of the Meghna.

mcqs.q: The Zuari river is in which state?
mcqs.e: Goa's two main rivers, the Mandovi and Zuari, both flow west.

mcqs.q: What caused the ancient Indo-Brahma river system to split into the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra?
o: Uplift in the Himalayan region during the Pleistocene
mcqs.e: Tectonic uplift (e.g. of the Potwar Plateau) during the Pleistocene broke up the Indo-Brahma river.

mcqs.q: Where do the Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab and Jhelum together join the Indus?
mcqs.e: These five rivers are together called the Panjnad.

mcqs.q: At which place does the Indus enter Ladakh?
mcqs.e: The Zanskar is a left-bank tributary of the Indus.

mcqs.q: Where does the Jhelum originate?
mcqs.e: It feeds Wular Lake.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
mcqs.e: The world's largest freshwater lake is Lake Superior (USA-Canada).

mcqs.q: Which is the largest tributary of the Indus by volume of water?
mcqs.e: The Chenab carries the most water among the Panjnad rivers; the Sutlej is the longest.

mcqs.q: Through which pass does the Sutlej enter India?
mcqs.e: The Sutlej rises near Rakshastal.

mcqs.q: By what name is the Sutlej known in Tibet?
mcqs.e: The Indus is the 'Lion's Mouth' and the Sutlej the 'Elephant's Mouth'.

mcqs.q: What is the ancient name of the Jhelum?
mcqs.e: The Greek name of the Jhelum is Hydaspes.

mcqs.q: What is the ancient name of the Chenab?
mcqs.e: Its Greek name is Acesines.

mcqs.q: What is the ancient name of the Ravi?
mcqs.e: The Greek name of the Ravi is Hydraotes.

mcqs.q: What is the ancient name of the Beas?
mcqs.e: The Greek name of the Beas is Hyphasis.

mcqs.q: What is the ancient name of the Sutlej?
mcqs.e: Its Greek name is Zaradros.

mcqs.q: Where does the Beas join the Sutlej?
mcqs.e: The Indira Gandhi Canal starts from Harike.

mcqs.q: Where does the Indira Gandhi Canal originate, and what is it also called?
mcqs.e: It is regarded as India's longest canal system.

mcqs.q: Why do most Peninsular rivers flow eastward?
o: The Peninsular plateau slopes towards the east
mcqs.e: The Narmada and Tapti are exceptions.

mcqs.q: Which two major rivers of Peninsular India flow westward?
mcqs.e: They flow through rift valleys.

mcqs.q: Flowing through rift valleys, what do the Narmada and Tapti form at their mouths?
mcqs.e: Low silt load and short courses prevent delta formation.

mcqs.q: The Narmada flows in a rift valley between which two ranges?
mcqs.e: The Vindhyas lie to the north and the Satpuras to the south.

mcqs.q: The Vindhya and Satpura ranges meet in which range?
mcqs.e: The Amarkantak plateau lies in the Maikal range.

mcqs.q: Where does the Narmada originate?
mcqs.e: Amarkantak is in the Maikal range.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest peak of the Satpura range (Mahadeo Hills)?
mcqs.e: Dhupgarh is about 1352 m high.

mcqs.q: Where does the Tapti originate?
mcqs.e: The Tapti flows south of the Satpura range.

mcqs.q: From the given options, the Tapti rises in which range?
mcqs.e: The Tapti rises on the Betul Plateau in the Satpuras.

mcqs.q: Which are tributaries of the Narmada?
mcqs.e: Trick: 'Tawe mein shakkar daalkar hila do'.

mcqs.q: Which river flows through a rift valley and passes near the Durgapur steel plant?
mcqs.e: The Damodar rises on the Chota Nagpur Plateau and joins the Hooghly.

mcqs.q: The Damodar is a tributary of:
mcqs.e: The Barakar is a tributary of the Damodar.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Teesta and Mahananda is correct?
o: Both are tributaries of the Brahmaputra
Both are tributaries of the Ganga
Teesta is a tributary of the Brahmaputra; Mahananda of the Ganga
Teesta is a tributary of the Ganga; Mahananda of the Brahmaputra
mcqs.e: The Teesta rises from Tso Lhamo Lake in Sikkim.

mcqs.q: Which of the following rivers does NOT rise on the Amarkantak Plateau?
mcqs.e: The Narmada, Son and Johila rise at Amarkantak.

mcqs.q: Which drainage pattern is shown by the Amarkantak Plateau?
mcqs.e: Rivers flow outward in all directions from a central high point.

mcqs.q: Which drainage pattern is the opposite of the radial pattern?
mcqs.e: Here rivers drain into a central lake or depression.

mcqs.q: What does a dendritic drainage pattern look like?
mcqs.e: Most Himalayan rivers of the Indus and Ganga systems show this pattern.

mcqs.q: In a trellis pattern, at what angle do tributaries join the main river?
mcqs.e: Tributaries meet the main stream almost perpendicularly.

mcqs.q: In which state is Loktak Lake, and what is it famous for?
mcqs.e: It is an example of centripetal drainage.

mcqs.q: Keibul Lamjao National Park is famous for:
o: Being a floating national park, home of the Sangai deer
mcqs.e: The Sangai (brow-antlered deer) is the state animal of Manipur.

mcqs.q: What are phumdis?
mcqs.e: Keibul Lamjao National Park is located on them.

mcqs.q: Which river flows through a small part of the Great Indian (Thar) Desert?
mcqs.e: The Luni rises in the Aravallis near Ajmer.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Luni river known?
mcqs.e: Its water is saline because evaporation exceeds rainfall.

mcqs.q: Where does the Luni river finally disappear?
mcqs.e: The Luni is the main inland river of Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Which is a major seasonal river of the Thar Desert region?
mcqs.e: Do not confuse the Ghaggar with the Ghaghara, a tributary of the Ganga.

mcqs.q: The Ghaggar river is found mainly in which regions?
mcqs.e: It is a monsoon-fed seasonal river.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Peninsular rivers flows eastward?
mcqs.e: The Sabarmati is in Gujarat and flows west.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest west-flowing river?
mcqs.e: The Tapti is the second-longest west-flowing river.

mcqs.q: The Mahanadi rises from which hills?
mcqs.e: The Mahanadi is mainly a river of Odisha.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a tributary of the Mahanadi?
mcqs.e: Mahanadi tributaries: Ong, Jonk, Tel, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib.

mcqs.q: Which dam is located on the Tapti?
mcqs.e: Ukai is in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: The Indira Sagar Dam is on which river?
mcqs.e: It is in Madhya Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest Peninsular river, also called the 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vriddha Ganga'?
mcqs.e: The Godavari is about 1465 km long.

mcqs.q: Where does the Godavari originate?
mcqs.e: The Western Ghats are called the Sahyadri in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Godavari?
mcqs.e: The Tungabhadra is a tributary of the Krishna.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct list of Godavari tributaries?
o: Manjira, Sabari, Purna, Penganga, Pranhita, Wainganga, Wardha, Indravati
mcqs.e: Trick: MS Dhoni, MS Subbulakshmi, PPP, WW, I.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is not a tributary of the Ganga but drains directly into the Bay of Bengal?
mcqs.e: The Mahanadi is an independent river.

mcqs.q: Which river is NOT a tributary of the Mahanadi?
mcqs.e: The Wardha is a tributary of the Godavari.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Brahmani and Baitarani rivers is correct?
o: They are tributaries of the Godavari
They are tributaries of the Ganga
They are independent rivers, not tributaries of any river
They are tributaries of the Mahanadi
mcqs.e: They drain into the Bay of Bengal north of the Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Subarnarekha river is correct?
o: It is a tributary of the Mahanadi
It is an independent river lying north of the Brahmani-Baitarani
It is a tributary of the Krishna
mcqs.e: It flows through Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal.

mcqs.q: The mouth of the Rushikulya river is famous for the mass nesting of:
mcqs.e: The mass nesting (arribada) of Olive Ridleys occurs on the Odisha coast.

mcqs.q: What is the effect of incubation temperature on turtle hatchlings?
o: Higher temperature gives females, lower gives males
Higher temperature gives males, lower gives females
mcqs.e: This is temperature-dependent sex determination.

mcqs.q: Which river is famous for ravine (badland) topography?
mcqs.e: The Chambal ravines are formed by gully erosion.

mcqs.q: Which type of erosion predominates in the Chambal, forming ravines?
mcqs.e: Cultivation is not possible in ravine land.

mcqs.q: Where does the Krishna originate?
mcqs.e: Mahabaleshwar is in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: Which are tributaries of the Krishna?
o: Bhima, Tungabhadra, Musi, Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Dudhganga
mcqs.e: Trick: 'Bhim tu Musi ko ghat pe le jaake maal receive kar, doodh aaya hai'.

mcqs.q: The Krishna basin extends mainly over which states?
o: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
mcqs.e: The Krishna does not flow through Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat or Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is located on which river?
mcqs.e: The Srisailam Dam is also on the Krishna.

mcqs.q: Which river forms a delta on the eastern coastal plain of India?
mcqs.e: West-flowing rivers form estuaries.

mcqs.q: What do west-flowing rivers form at their mouths?
mcqs.e: The Mandovi, Zuari, Periyar and Bharathapuzha are west-flowing rivers.

mcqs.q: Which are the two major west-flowing rivers of Kerala?
mcqs.e: They rise in the Western Ghats and drain into the Arabian Sea.

mcqs.q: Where does the Kaveri originate?
mcqs.e: It lies in the Brahmagiri range of the Western Ghats.

mcqs.q: Which are tributaries of the Kaveri?
mcqs.e: The Indravati is a tributary of the Godavari, not the Kaveri.

mcqs.q: The Indravati river is a tributary of:
mcqs.e: Do not link it to the Kaveri just because of the '-vati' ending.

mcqs.q: Which dam is built on the Pennar river?
mcqs.e: The Pennar is an east-flowing river of Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: Which east-flowing river of Tamil Nadu flows through Madurai?
mcqs.e: Madurai lies on the Vaigai; the Tamirabarani flows further south.

mcqs.q: Which three hill ranges form the Western Ghats in southern India?
mcqs.e: Anamudi (Anamalai) is the highest peak among them.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate height of Anamudi?
mcqs.e: Anamudi is the highest peak of Peninsular India.

mcqs.q: Doddabetta peak lies in which hills?
mcqs.e: Its height is about 2637 m.

mcqs.q: The word 'monsoon' is derived from a word of which language?
mcqs.e: It means the seasonal reversal of winds.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'monsoon'?
mcqs.e: The Arabic word 'mausim' means season.

mcqs.q: On 21 June, the Sun's rays fall vertically on the:
mcqs.e: In May-June, north India and the Tibetan Plateau become intensely heated.

mcqs.q: What does the heated Tibetan Plateau create in summer?
mcqs.e: Tibet is called the 'Roof of the World'.

mcqs.q: Which jet stream plays a role in forming the monsoon trough?
mcqs.e: The monsoon trough creates a low-pressure zone that draws in winds.

mcqs.q: Which force deflects the direction of the south-west monsoon?
mcqs.e: The south-east trades cross the equator and are deflected to the right.

mcqs.q: In the Northern Hemisphere, the Coriolis force deflects moving objects to the:
mcqs.e: In the Southern Hemisphere, deflection is to the left.

mcqs.q: Where is the Coriolis force zero and where is it maximum?
o: Zero at the equator, maximum at the poles
Maximum at the equator, zero at the poles
mcqs.e: For winds, this deflection is also stated as Ferrel's Law.

mcqs.q: What is the high-pressure area east of Madagascar called?
mcqs.e: This high pushes winds towards the low pressure over India.

mcqs.q: Which branch of the monsoon brings rain to the west coast?
mcqs.e: It strikes the Western Ghats and causes heavy rainfall.

mcqs.q: What are the three sub-branches of the Arabian Sea branch of the south-west monsoon?
o: One striking the Western Ghats, one along the Narmada, one parallel to the Aravallis
Towards the Thar, parallel to the Indus
Towards the Himalaya, parallel to the Ganga
mcqs.e: Blowing parallel to the Aravallis, it brings little rain to the Thar.

mcqs.q: Where do the Arabian Sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch meet?
mcqs.e: The two branches merge over the Punjab plains.

mcqs.q: Mawsynram, famous for the highest rainfall in the world, lies in which hills?
mcqs.e: The Bay of Bengal branch causes heavy rain on the Meghalaya Plateau.

mcqs.q: Tura, which can receive in one day the rainfall Jaisalmer gets in 10 years, is located in:
mcqs.e: Tura is in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya.

mcqs.q: What does the 'burst' of the monsoon mean?
o: A gap of several days in rainfall
Sudden onset of heavy rain at the start of the monsoon
mcqs.e: A 'break' means a dry spell in the rainfall.

mcqs.q: What does a 'break' in the monsoon mean?
o: A dry spell between rainy periods
mcqs.e: Burst = the sudden onset of monsoon rains.

mcqs.q: In winter, which wind system brings rain to the Coromandel Coast?
mcqs.e: These winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and bring it to land.

mcqs.q: The retreating monsoon is also known as the:
mcqs.e: Withdrawal of the monsoon begins from the north-west.

mcqs.q: From which part of India does the withdrawal of the monsoon begin?
mcqs.e: The withdrawal begins in September.

mcqs.q: What causes winter rainfall in north India?
mcqs.e: They are brought from the Mediterranean by the westerly jet stream.

mcqs.q: Where do Western Disturbances originate?
mcqs.e: They benefit rabi crops, especially wheat.

mcqs.q: What is the local name in Rajasthan for winter rain caused by Western Disturbances?
mcqs.e: It is considered good for the rabi crop.

mcqs.q: At roughly what height do jet streams blow?
mcqs.e: These winds blow at very high speeds.

mcqs.q: When does the south-west monsoon normally enter India?
o: In the first week of June (Kerala)
In the first week of July
mcqs.e: It usually covers the whole country by about mid-July.

mcqs.q: What is the duration of the south-west monsoon season in India?
mcqs.e: October-November is the retreating monsoon season.

mcqs.q: What is 'October Heat'?
mcqs.e: Clear skies and high humidity make the weather oppressive.

mcqs.q: What causes the humid heat of October (October Heat)?
o: Clear skies and evaporation of moisture from the land
mcqs.e: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: What is the full form of ITCZ?
mcqs.e: It is the zone where the trade winds converge.

mcqs.q: What is the literal meaning of 'El Nino'?
mcqs.e: It refers to a rise in sea surface temperature in the Pacific Ocean.

mcqs.q: What is El Nino?
o: A cyclone in the Indian Ocean
A rise in sea surface temperature of the Pacific Ocean
A fall in Pacific Ocean temperature
mcqs.e: It weakens the monsoon in India.

mcqs.q: What is the usual effect of El Nino on the Indian monsoon?
mcqs.e: It recurs at intervals of about 3 to 7 years.

mcqs.q: What does La Nina mean for India?
o: Above-normal rainfall, favourable for the monsoon
mcqs.e: In La Nina, Pacific Ocean temperatures fall below normal.

mcqs.q: Why are fishing grounds off the coast of Peru affected in an El Nino year?
o: Cold water does not upwell, so phytoplankton decline
mcqs.e: Accumulated warm water stops the upwelling of nutrients.

mcqs.q: During El Nino, what are the rainfall conditions in the eastern Pacific (Peru) and the western Pacific (Australia)?
o: Rain near Peru, deficit in Australia/India
mcqs.e: Warm water shifts back towards the eastern Pacific.

mcqs.q: What is the main reason the monsoon trough intensifies over north India by the end of May?
mcqs.e: Heating makes air rise, creating low pressure.

mcqs.q: What are the violent pre-monsoon evening thunderstorms of north-east India called?
mcqs.e: In West Bengal they are called Kalbaisakhi.

mcqs.q: What are Nor'westers called in West Bengal?
mcqs.e: 'Kal' means calamity, and the name refers to the month of Baisakh.

mcqs.q: What are Nor'westers called in Assam?
mcqs.e: They are beneficial for jute cultivation.

mcqs.q: What are the pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and coastal Karnataka that help ripen mangoes called?
mcqs.e: They help in the ripening of mangoes.

mcqs.q: What are the showers that help coffee flowers blossom called?
mcqs.e: They occur in Kerala and Karnataka.

mcqs.q: What are the main varieties of coffee?
mcqs.e: In India, coffee is grown mainly in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Which state is the largest producer of jute in India?
mcqs.e: Bangladesh is a major exporter of jute.

mcqs.q: What is the main cause of the Loo?
mcqs.e: The Loo is a hot, dry wind that blows in summer.

mcqs.q: What role does the subtropical jet stream play in the withdrawal of the monsoon?
o: Subsidence and formation of high pressure, triggered by the southward shift of the ITCZ
mcqs.e: The ITCZ shifts as the Sun moves southward.

mcqs.q: What are the latitudes around 30 degrees N and 30 degrees S called?
mcqs.e: The calm zone near the equator is called the Doldrums.

mcqs.q: What is the calm wind zone near the equator called?
mcqs.e: This is the region of the ITCZ.

mcqs.q: What are the strong westerlies between 40 and 60 degrees S latitudes called?
o: Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Shrieking Sixties
mcqs.e: They are very strong because there is little landmass there.

mcqs.q: What are the three main types of rainfall?
mcqs.e: Orographic rainfall is also called relief rainfall.

mcqs.q: In 'orographic rainfall', what does 'oro' mean?
mcqs.e: It is also called relief rainfall.

mcqs.q: The side of a mountain where air rises and causes more rainfall is called the:
mcqs.e: The opposite side is the rain-shadow area.

mcqs.q: Which of the following lies in a rain-shadow area?
mcqs.e: Pune lies on the eastern (leeward) side of the Western Ghats.

mcqs.q: Why does the Thar Desert receive little rainfall?
o: Winds blow parallel to the Aravallis, lack moisture and find no water sources over land
mcqs.e: The Arabian Sea branch passes parallel to the Aravallis.

mcqs.q: Which part of mainland India receives over 200 cm of average annual rainfall?
mcqs.e: Ladakh is a cold desert and the Thar is a hot desert.

mcqs.q: What type of forests are found in the Western Ghats?
mcqs.e: Heavy rainfall supports evergreen forests here.

mcqs.q: What type of desert is Ladakh?
mcqs.e: The Thar is a hot desert.

mcqs.q: What is the gap in the Western Ghats between the Nilgiri and Anamalai hills called?
mcqs.e: It lies between Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
